Jasmine — adding technical detail on the canary windows and capacity expectations. See proposed schedule attached (canary-schedule-v1.csv). Highlights:

- Dedicated pool sizing: recommend reserved pool for initial canary of 2 x A100 equivalent instances to ensure stable tail latency during traffic ramp (we can convert to your preferred instance sizing).
- Canary traffic ramp: 1% -> 5% over first 2 hours (30m steps), then 10% -> 25% over next 6 hours (hourly checks). Final 50% -> 100% over 24 hours contingent on telemetry.
- Success criteria: 99th percentile latency within X ms of baseline, error rate < 0.1% sustained for 30 minutes, no degradation in token-level QA metrics beyond configured thresholds.
- Warm-up: pre-warm KV cache with synthetic traffic for 30 minutes prior to sending live traffic.

Risks/Notes:
- If your traffic has long-context tails, we recommend an additional warm-up window and temporary max-seq limit to reduce OOM risk while quantized models are being validated.
- For private deployments (VPC), we advise enabling native flow logs for the first 72 hours of production traffic.

Attaching: canary-schedule-v1.csv

Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Redwood Dedicated

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Adding integration and API contract specifics for the appendix response. See inline snippets below (I also attached integration-contract-snippets.txt):

- API versioning: We will support stable v1 endpoints for the entire rollout. Backward-compatible changes only; any breaking changes will be released under v2 and feature flagged. Consumers can pin model versions via the API (model=redwood-llama2:2027-06).
- Telemetry signals (sent by default): request_id, model_version, route_latency_ms, token_count, error_type. We'll provide a small telemetry dashboard template (Grafana) and the alert thresholds used in the canary success criteria.
- Authentication: TLS 1.2+ with mTLS optional for private, token-based bearer auth for hosted; recommend rotating service tokens every 90 days.
- KV cache warm-up: provide endpoint to pre-populate session prefixes; we recommend 30m synthetic traffic as Ben noted.
- Data residency & drift: customer data does not persist in long-term store on hosted; session KV for streaming is ephemeral and retained per config (default 24h). For Private, data residency follows customer storage.
- Rollback: automatic route-switching to previous stable model variant + traffic cut to failover pool. Manual rollback procedure documented in runbook with steps and expected RTO ~5 minutes for traffic cut.

Staging -> Canary gates:
- Integration smoke tests (API contract, auth, cert, basic generation)
- End-to-end test harness run (sample prompts)
- Telemetry sanity check (alerts cleared)

I'll sync the exact API example snippets into the consolidated PDF.

Karthik
Senior Product Engineer, Serving Runtime

Emily — attaching our consolidated response (Alphasecure_Response_AppendixB.pdf). Summary highlights below and linked artifacts:

Summary (high level):
- Timeline: typical end-to-end onboarding target = 6 weeks from contract signature. Proposed milestone cadence: Week 0: Kickoff & network prep; Week 1-2: Dev integration & smoke tests; Week 3: Staging validation & pre-canary; Week 4: Canary (48h active ramp + 24h observation); Week 5-6: Production cutover & monitoring; final acceptance at Week 6. Exact dates can be adjusted per your capacity calendar.
- Canary: staged ramp 1% -> 5% (2h) -> 10% -> 25% (6h) -> 50% (24h) -> 100% (24h). Automated success checks include latency & error SLAs and a model-quality regression test suite (prompt set provided). Rollback triggers and manual cutover steps are included in the attached runbook.
- Capacity & scaling: initial reserved pool recommended per canary (Ben's note); autoscaling policy configured for production with headroom to absorb 2x typical daily peak for 72h post-cutover.
- Network & security: VPC peering, allowlist ranges, TLS + optional mTLS for private deploys. We will provide a firewall checklist and cert instructions (see page 4 of attached PDF).
- Operational runbooks: included are escalation contacts, on-call rotation handoff template, and a step-by-step manual rollback section. Expected RTO for a traffic cut is ~5 minutes; full recovery time depends on root cause but initial mitigation is immediate traffic reroute to failover pool.

Attached: Alphasecure_Response_AppendixB.pdf (consolidated answers), canary-schedule-v1.csv, integration-contract-snippets.txt.
